Reade-97.bio: [[Category:Edinburgh, Scotland]] [[Category:Maryland, Immigrants from Scotland]] [[Category:Calvert County, Province of Maryland]] ==Preface== ===Place of Birth=== New information regarding George's land ownership of “Reidbourne” revealed that he was born a Reid in Scotland and had a brother, Alexander. [See Reference Notes: Reidbourne] ===Surname Spelling=== The surname Read, Reade, etc. were the English and/or phonetic spellings of his Scottish surname of Reid. 17th century secretarial script is often misinterpreted, so the original may actually be an “i” for the “e” and the ending “e” may have just been a flourish. In fact, at least one court document has both spellings in the same document. Jane and Bob Wolfe Genealogy https://websites.umich.edu/~bobwolfe/gen/pn/p22501.htm Citing: Archives of Maryland Online, Provincial Court Land Records, Volume 721, page 39, of 39-48, MSA S552-8, TL 2 SM 22-11, [MD Archives]. And Archives of Maryland Online, Provincial Court Land Records, Volume 680, page 1074, index entry citing Lib. P.L. No. 5 (17254), Deed, p. 40 and 43, [MD Archives] Accessed 3 September 2024. Proceedings of the Provincial Court, 1679-1680/1; Volume 69, Preface 18; Archives of Maryland Online https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc2900/sc2908/000001/000069/html/am69p--18.html Accessed 31 August 2024. https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc2900/sc2908/000001/000721/html/am721--39.html Accessed 1 September 2024. ===Maryland County Formation=== The counties in the Colony of Maryland saw many boundary changes, name changes and additions during Maryland's early years. For example, the east-northeast part of St. Mary's County, the original county in Maryland, became Patuxent County in 1654 and part of Patuxent County became Charles County in 1658. Also in this year, Patuxent's name changed to Calvert. “History of County Formations in Maryland 1637-1997” https://homepages.rootsweb.com/~george/countyformations/marylandformationmaps.html and https://homepages.rootsweb.com/~george/countyformations/marylandformationmaps.html Accessed 17 September 2024. So although George's properties remained in the same location, they were at some point in 4 different counties. George arrived in the Colony of Maryland about 1658 and died in 1666, placing his residence in Calvert County. [[Brown-18795|Beth (Brown) Golden]] 23 September 2024. ==Biography== ===1629 Birth and Parents=== George Reid was born to John Reid and Helen Henryson [Henderson] on 1 January 1629 in Edinburgh. His known brothers, all baptized in Edinburgh Parish, were:Scotland's People, Old Parish Registers, Births and Baptisms. https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/church-registers/church-births-baptisms Accessed 3 September 2024. [See Research Notes: Reid - Mackall Family Connections for further family details] #William, 28 November 1624 #John, 5 February 1626 #Alexander, 1 January 1629, his twin [parents listed in Scotland's People as Johnne Reid and Elspeth Jamesone, but this is likely a church clerk or transcription error. No record has been transcribed by FreeReg.UK to compare. #William, 22 January 1632 (the first William presumably died young) #Clement, 29 September 1634 #Margaret, 25 July 1637 ===Before Maryland=== Since George was not the first son of John Reid, he did not receive the benefits of primogeniture and would have had to establish his own status and wealth. Although many men with the surname Reid attended the University of Edinburgh, it does not appear that George was among them. A Catalogue of the Graduates in the Faculties of Arts; University of Edinburgh, Neil and Co., 1858. Google Ebook https://play.google.com/books/reader?id=Lz1DAAAAYAAJ&pg=GBS.PA74&hl=en Accessed 21 September 2024. There are several men named George Reid who were members of the Edinburgh Burgess and Guild, but none appear to be the subject of this biography.Watson, Charles Boog. Roll of Edinburgh Burgesses and Guild Brethren; Google Books https://www.google.com/books/edition/Roll_of_Edinburgh_Burgesses_and_Guild_br/h2sZAAAAIAAJ?hl=en Accessed 21 September 2024. He may have traveled to London for greater opportunities and this is how he became employed by [[Eltonhead-41|Edward Eltonhead (bef.1610-1660)]], who was the Master of the Chancery among other prestigious roles before his death in 1660. [See his profile for more details] If Gibb's statement, “served” regarding George's arrival in Maryland [See Section: About 1656 Arrival in Maryland] meant that George was an indentured servant of Eltonhead, he would have arrived in London about 1650, allowing the usual 7 years of indenture to expire. ===First Marriage=== 4 marriage records were found for George Reid in Edinburgh between 1649 (presuming he was 20 at time of marriage) and 1658. Of these, the most likely is Rebecca Dowgall [Dougall] who he married in Edinburgh on 7 July 1653. George was listed as a merchant. No burial record was found for Rebecca in Edinburgh, making her the best choice of the 4.Midlothian : Edinburgh : The Parish Church : Transcript : "Parish Register" database, FreeREG (https://www.freereg.org.uk/search_records/5818220be93790eb7f3caac0 : viewed 4 Sep 2024) marriage George Reid to Rebecca Dougall 07 Jul 1653 Accessed 3 September 2024. She died during the crossing of the Atlantic or after their arrival in Calvert County between 1656 and about 1658, when he married Alice Taylor, widow of Samuel Griffin. However, if George married in London, one record was found which possibly pertains to him. “George Reade” married Joane Plowman in St. Botolph's Church, London on 28 September 1653. Note that others associated with George in Maryland also worshiped here: Griffin, Holloway, Taylor, Tyllie and Nuthall, to name just a few.London (City) : Bishopsgate : St Botolph : Transcript : "Parish Register" database, FreeREG (https://www.freereg.org.uk/search_records/581814abe93790eb7f28d151 : viewed 21 Sep 2024) marriage George Reade to Joane Plowman 28 Sep 1653 Whoever his first wife was, she either died during the crossing of the Atlantic or after their arrival in Calvert County sometime before 1658, when he married Alice Taylor, widow of Samuel Griffin. ===About 1656 Arrival in Maryland=== George, possibly with his wife, arrived in Maryland in 1656. == Biography == ===Birth=== Alice Taylor was likely born in England, most likely in the area of Houndsditch Lane, London, England sometime between 1620 and 1630. This estimate is based on her brother, Robert's, birth year of about 1621 and a 1656 court record. [See Birth Family, Court Records and Research Notes: London Parish Records and St. Botolph's Church, Bishopsgate, London, England.] Note that no birth or marriage records were found in Scotland between 1600 and 1660 for Alice Taylor and Samuel Griffin with spelling variations on surname. Because of the Griffin family association with Catherine Griffin Sprigg, a part of Alice's wider family circle, who came from Gloucestershire to London and the colonies, those baptismal records were also checked. Many members of the Taylor and Griffin families were born in Gloucestershire between 1558 and 1640, but no records were found for Alice Taylor or Samuel Griffin.FreeReg.uk https://www.freereg.org.uk/ Accessed 9 October 2024. Also part of Alice's wider family circle, were Elizabeth Tyllie and John Holloway. They were both from Gloucestershire and moved to the City of London prior to going to the Colony of Virginia.Golden, Beth. No Will or Inventory has been found as of 10 October 2024.[See Research Notes: Mortality in the British North American Colonies] ==Research Notes== === Mortality in the British North American Colonies=== Nearly 35 to 40 percent of early colonials died soon after their arrival due to a condition known as seasoning with the average age of men dying at 45 years. This condition was due primarily to the adjustment of settlers to the drastic change from their home environment, including diseases like malaria, yellow fever, smallpox and others due to no running water or plumbing, adverse weather and wet conditions living along rivers, marshes, etc. Alice may also have died from pregnancy or child-birth complications.King, Julia and Douglas H. Ubelaker, eds. Living and Dying on the 17th Century Patuxent Frontier; he Maryland Historical Trust Press, Crownsville, MD. pp. 6-7 https://jefpat.maryland.gov/Documents/mac-lab/king-douglas-living-and-dying-on-the-17th-century-patuxent-frontier.pdf Citing Lorean Walsh (1977:129-130 and Menard, Russell R. (1975a). Economy and Society in Early Colonial Maryland. Unpublished Ph.D. dissertation, Department of History, University of Iowa. Accessed 5 October 2024. Wikipedia Disease in Colonial America https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disease_in_colonial_America Accessed 5 October 2024. Conditions in the Early Colonies Smithsonian's The Secret in the Cellar Webcomic, an educational resource from the Written in Bone exhibition, February 2009 – 2014. https://naturalhistory.si.edu/sites/default/files/media/file/wibconditionsearlycoloniesfinal.pdf Accessed 5 October 2024. ===London Parish Records=== Parish Registers: From 1538, the parish clergy were legally required to keep registers recording all baptisms, marriages, and burials which occurred in their churches (or burial grounds).Despite their apparently comprehensive coverage, it is important to note that parish registers suffered from a significant degree of underregistration. Those who were not members of the Anglican Church, particularly dissenters, often did not register these events, espeically marriages, with their Anglican clergyman. It is is also important to note that there was often a delay between births and baptisms, and the births of infants who died before they were baptised were often not reported. Clandestine marriages, which took place outside the parish, were not recorded in parish registers, though the incidence of these fell dramatically following the passage of the 1694 Marriage Duty Act, which imposed heavy fines for non-registration of marriages (though with one centre of clandestine marriages, Holy Trinity Minories, immediately adjacent to St Botolph Aldgate, this possibility should not be ignored). Finally not all deaths in a parish led to burials within the parish, since some bodies were returned by parish officers to the individual's parish of settlement, or by families to a family vault in another parish. Levels of underregistration varied from parish to parish, and by type of event. It has been estimated that in late seventeenth-century London, birth under-registrations caused by religious dissent were about 17 per cent of all births, with a further unknown percentage of births missing due to infant mortality before baptism. In contrast, the underregistration of marriages, particularly after 1694, and deaths, was considerably lower. While there is no reason to question the accuracy of the data provided, the fact an event was not recorded in a parish register does not mean it did not happen in the parish.London Lives https://www.londonlives.org/static/LSDSPAR.jsp#fn1_1 Accessed 8 October 2024. ===St. Botolph Church without Bishopsgate, London, England=== Circumstantial evidence suggests that Alice Taylor was born in London and baptized in St. Botolph Church, without Bishopsgate. Families associated with Alice in Maryland also worshiped here: Griffin, Thickpenny (owned land adjacent to Samuel Griffin and subsequently George Reid; Henry transported to the Colony of Maryland by Robert Taylor, brother of Alice Taylor Griffin ReidCarr, Lois. St. Mary's Mens Career Files https://msa.maryland.gov/megafile/msa/speccol/sc5000/sc5094/004000/004082/html/sc5094-4082-09.html Accessed 9 October 2024.), Sprigg (Joane Sprigg, daughter of Thomas Sprigg succeeded Alice as George Reid's wife; as well as the associated families of Beall (spelling variations, Joane Sprigg also married Mr. Beall), Holloway, Tyllie and Nuthall), Mountney (spelling variations, Joane Sprigg also married Mr. Mountney, Mr. Beall and Mr. Taylor) and finally Platte and Rhodes (transported by Samuel Griffin to Calvert County, Colony of Maryland). (p. 17) *Tailour, Robert (fl. 1583), cordwainer. 43/7/2 (poss 1583) In April 1583, two months after the expiration date of Bartholomew Pytman's 17 1/2-year term in the Three Tuns, Robert Tailour, cordwainer, and Samson Denacome, tanner, brought a writ of right patent against Bartholomew concerning 2 messuages with appurtenances in the parish of St. Botolph Aldgate. His wife, Mary continued to live in the property until at least 1674-75. p. 183ST. BOTOLPH ALDGATE GAZETTEER https://sas-space.sas.ac.uk/9355/1/St%20Botolph%20Aldgate%20Minories%20Gazetteer.pdf The two St. Botolph churches are about .5 miles apart with Bishopsgate lying at the north and Houndsditch Lane (route A1211) basically connecting them. Because of their proximity, the Taylor and other associated families could have worshiped in either church. Both parishes are located on the eastern of the city of London, between London and Middlesex.St. Botolph Aldgate; London Lives, 1690 – 1800 https://www.londonlives.org/static/StBotolphAldgate.jsp Accessed 6 October 2024. In 1593, this area was not heavily settled and developed.Plan of the City of London in the Time of Queen Elizabeth 1593 http://mapco.net/london/1593elizabethb.htm Accessed 6 October 2024. The majority of the dwellings were tenements.For a description, see Dr. Mark Latham, ST. BOTOLPH ALDGATE140-141 HOUNDSDITCH, EAST SIDE https://sas-space.sas.ac.uk/4602/1/Property_History_Narratives_%28sample%29.pdf Records for the members of these families who remained in the London area are also numerous and can be found in London Lives databases. This little street is now known as Middlesex Street, located .2 miles northeast of Houndsditch Lane. The Holloway, Tyllie, Nuthall and Graves families lived along Houndsditch in the 17th century. == Biography ==

There are quite a few John Bruces' baptised in Scotland between 1670 and 1680.  The biggest problem is knowing which one came down to Halifax about 1700.  See the Research Notes for some of the baptisms.

John Bruce married Constant  Kendall on 20th April, 1704 at Halifax, Yorkshire, England.

John Bruce and Constant had the following children:
*Richard John Bruce baptised 2nd January 1704 at Hallifax (Halifax)
*Thomas Bruce baptised November 1706 at St. John the Baptist Halifax
* Margarett Bruce baptised April 1709- father- John Bruce of Hall. (Halifax)
*Martha Bruce baptised 20th September 1709 at Halifax
*Mary Bruce baptised 4th April, 1711 at Halifax
*Constant Bruce baptised 13th June 1712 - father - John Bruce of Hall. (Halifax)

It appears that Constant Bruce passed away in childbirth.  Constant was buried 13th June 1712 at St John the Baptist Halifax,  wife of John Bruce of Hall. (Halifax).

John Bruce remarried to Mary Fletcher on 27th November 1715 at Halifax. The parish register entry states that John Bruce  is from Midgley and that his is a Taylor (Tailor).  Mary is from Hall. ( Halifax) and that she is a spinster. 

Mary Bruce passed away September 1751 and was interred on the 20th September 1751at St John the Baptist, Halifax.  The parish register entry of the burial states that Mary is the wife of John Bruce, a Taylor (Tailor). of Hx. (Halifax).

John Bruce passed away in December 1755, and was buried 31st December 1755 at St. James Halifax, Yorkshire, England.

==Research Notes==

*Quite a few of the personal family histories on Ancestry and My Heritage websites  suggest that John Bruce was baptised, on various dates between 1676 and 1682  in Little Stream, Arboath, Argyllshire.  I have not located any evidence of any baptism for John Bruce to support this suggestion.

*There is a baptism of a John Bruce on the 14th August 1677 in Dundee, Angus, Scotland to parents - John Bruce and Margaret Smith. (Note:  Arboath is about 17 miles (27kms) north-east of Dundee).

* Another good candidate is John Bruce baptised 7th August 1677 in Kilconquhar, Fife, Scotland to parents - John Bruce and Christin Archibald

*John Bruce baptised 30th June 1677 in Alloa, Clackmannan, Clackmannanshire, Scotland to parents - John Bruce and Agnis Finlasone

*My personal favourite is John Bruce baptised 4th January 1673 at Clackmannan to parents - John Bruce and Margaret Liddell.

*Most personal family histories seem to agree that a John Bruce was baptised sometime between 1673 and 1682 and that he came down to Halifax about 1700.  If anyone has any sources or information that can confirm who his parents were and support when John came to Halifax,  it would  be welcomed.

Janet Glasgow is represented on WikiTree as the wife of James Woodside. Her reported dates and Irish birthplace have not been established by a reviewed original record.

== Research Notes ==

[[Glasgow-1498|John Glasgow]] is documented as a survivor of the 1679 ''Croune of London'' wreck under Cavers parish, Scotland. An earlier profile version placed Janet's death at Elgin, Illinois, in 1775. This is impossible because Elgin was founded in 1835; the city history is retained below as evidence for excluding that location. The generic baptism collection and memorial previously cited do not supply an original record proving Janet's Irish birth or her father.

[[Category:Albemarle, North Carolina]] [[Category:Tyrrell County, North Carolina]] [[Category:Chowan County, North Carolina]] == Biography == {{US Southern Colonist Sticker|Carolina}} Mary may have been born about 1670 in Chowan, North Carolina. Her father has been identified as William Mitchell, however, his profile is unsourced and incongruent in terms of a North Carolina affiliation. Her first husband was John Harrison, by whom they had five children:Barrow, Lee G. [https://www.familysearch.org/en/memories/memory/213012680?cid=mem_copy My Everitt Family: Chowan and Tyrrell County, North Carolina; Southeast Georgia.] 2014. Gainesville, Georgia: Author. # William Harrison # John Harrison # Elizabeth (Harrison) Long, possibly married Thomas Long # Thomas Harrison # Hannah (Harrison) Gerkin, who married Zachariah Gerkin A 1720 Chowan County deed (Deed Book C1, p. 4) names Mary, who had secondly married Nathaniel Everitt by circa 1701. Among their children mentioned in this 1720 deed: # Mary (Everitt) Stubbs (circa 1701-1738) who married Thomas Stubbs # Elizabeth (Everitt) Blount Ray (born circa 1703) who married Benjamin Blount as her first husband, and secondly William Ray # Sarah (Everitt) Jordan Gerkin Fagan (circa 1705-1783) who married as her first husband William Jordan (died about 1738 - although the Barrow narrative relays this information based on William Jordan's 1732 will stating that Nathaniel Everett was appointed guardian for the children of his eldest daughter'' - which would seem to be Mary, not Sarah), secondly Zachariah Gerkin (same as Hannah (Harrison) Gerkin?), and thirdly married Richard Fagan # Nathaniel (1707-1782) who married Elizabeth unknown [FamilySearch shows her as Elizabeth Hayward (30 Jun 1704, Medon, Worcester, Massachusetts Bay Colony-1763, Salem, Essex, Massachusetts Bay Colony)]; received his father's estate by a 1744 deed Mary died at the age of about 68 in 1738. == Research Notes == * ''My Everitt Family: Chowan and Tyrrell County, North Carolina; Southeast Georgia,'' (2014) cites two secondary sources. The document is provided on FamilySearch by contributor-user author Lee Barrow, placed as a Memory for Margarete (Burk) Everett (born 1745), wife of Jehu Evertt (1740-1824), a grandson by Nathaniel Everett "Sr," (1707-1782) on FamilySearch. Several of the stated facts in Barrow's narrative appear to need sorting at minimum, and direct ties to primary citations to help clarify relationships and the timeline, and these are listed below. Until definitive validation of the relationships and timeline is made, the profile is essentially unsourced and speculative: ** Alvaretta Kenan Register. Everett/Everitt family: a genealogical history. 1987. '''Book''': '''NOTE: Index Only""" ''Catalog Record: Everett/Everitt family: a genealogical history | HathiTrust Digital Library''
[https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/005714523 HathiTrust] (accessed 21 October 2025). Note that '''Alvaretta Kenan Register Papers, 1700-1985,''' part of the University of North Carolina: Chapel Hill is housed in their Southern Historical Collection, which reports that ''Everett/Everitt Family (1987), a genealogical study by Alvaretta Kenan Register,'' [was] published posthumously by the estate of Alvaretta Kenan Register. ** Bailey, Jane Stubbs & Everett, Vernon L Jr. [http://www.familysearch.org/library/books/idurl/1/466251 ''Nathaniel and Mary (Mitchell) Harrison Everett: of Tyrrell (now Washington) County, North Carolina and some of their descendants and related families.''] Vol. 1 & 2. 2001. Plymouth, North Carolina: J S Bailey. Limited searching available at FamilySearch link. * This spouse of Nathaniel may in fact be an amalgamation, especially considering that other researchers concluded that his wife's maiden name was unknown. * She is attached to a son by her husband of the same name. His dates are reported as certain by at least one researcher (Barrow, 2014). Thus, her birth date was adjusted so that it would not be out of range for her having a child in 1707. Barrow reports that his wife was Mary (Mitchell) Harrison, daughter of William Mitchell and widow of John Harrison. Barrow reports that Mary (Mitchell) Harrison and John Harrison had five children. Lastly, Barrow reports that in a 1720 deed, Nathaniel and his wife Mary had as their children: # Mary (Everitt) Stubbs (about 1701-738) who married Thomas Stubbs # Elizabeth (Everitt) Blount Ray (about 1703) # Sarah (Everitt) Jordan Gerkin Fagan (about 1705-1783) who married William Jordan, 2nd married Zachariah Gerkin, and 3rd married Richard Fagan # Nathaniel Everitt (1707-1782) who married Elizabeth Unknown * Mary (Mitchell) Harrison Everitt on FamilySearch (1660-1744) has no sources that are a clear or definitive match: {{FamilySearch|2H2Q-ZW3}} * Previous connection to Bowlers has been deemed in error. == Sources == == Acknowledgments == * Profile Bowlers-1 was created through the import of dad_2012-08-01.ged on Aug 1, 2012 by [[Stroud-316 | John Stroud]].
